paper_metadata.title: Treatment and challenges with antiepileptic drugs in patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study utilized a population-based recruitment strategy covering a specific geographic region (Buskerud County) and achieved a high participation rate (69% of all GGE patients), which is excellent for this type of study. The inclusion/exclusion criteria and baseline characteristics are well-defined.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Drammen Hospital serves all patients with epilepsy in Buskerud County, covering 9% of the Norwegian population.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as the epilepsy patients within a specific Norwegian county served by a single hospital.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Recruitment of patients was based on a search of medical records containing an International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) code of epilepsy (G40) at Drammen Hospital during 1999– 2013.
items.reasoning: The use of ICD-10 codes and a centralized hospital record system provides a robust sampling frame.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: medical record search... during 1999– 2013. The clinical interviews were conducted between November 2016 and August 2018
items.reasoning: Both the retrospective identification period and the prospective interview period are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Drammen Hospital... Buskerud County, covering 9% of the Norwegian population.
items.reasoning: The geographic and institutional setting is clearly defined.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included patients who would most likely be diagnosed with JME within the period of the medical record search, i.e., those younger than 40 years and older than 14 years. All patients diagnosed with genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE) were invited to participate
items.reasoning: Age and diagnosis-based criteria are clearly provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: All patients diagnosed with genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE) were invited to participate, where 69% accepted
items.reasoning: A 69% participation rate from a population-based sample is considered high and adequate to limit selection bias.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Ninety patients with defined JME diagnosis, 54/36 women/men aged 14-39 (mean: 25) years, were included.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the results section provide age, gender, age at onset, and seizure types.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As this was a cross-sectional assessment (questionnaire/interview) of a cohort identified from records, the primary concern is the initial participation rate (69%), which was high. There is no evidence of significant loss to follow-up within the analysis phase.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.evidence_snippet: Ninety patients were classified as having JME and included.
items.reasoning: The study analyzed the full sample of those who consented and met the JME criteria.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (AED use) were verified through medical records, which is a highly reliable method compared to self-report alone. The definitions of the drugs and their use (mono vs polytherapy) are clear.

items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Data regarding AEDs were confirmed from medical records at Drammen Hospital, Norway (2007–2018).
items.reasoning: AED use is clearly defined and verified via clinical records.

items.evidence_snippet: Each participant's hospital record was thoroughly reviewed in order to confirm information concerning medical history, including previous AED use.
items.reasoning: Verification against medical records significantly reduces recall bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Eighty-four percent of the patients used 1–3 AEDs as their current therapy (Table 2).
items.reasoning: Categorization of AED use (monotherapy vs polytherapy) is standard and not data-driven.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary outcome (seizure freedom) relied on patient self-report via questionnaire and interview. While this is common in epilepsy research, it is subject to recall bias. However, the study did distinguish between GTCS and myoclonic jerks, which adds granularity.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The dependent variable was being without GTCS for more than one year (yes or no).
items.reasoning: Seizure freedom is clearly defined with a specific timeframe (1 year).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Information about... seizure outcome... was obtained directly from the patient.
items.reasoning: Self-reporting is standard but less reliable than a prospective seizure diary or objective monitoring.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: A semistructured questionnaire designed for the purpose of this study was used
items.reasoning: All participants were assessed using the same questionnaire and interview framework.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study performed multivariable logistic regression to account for age and gender when assessing the impact of specific AEDs on GTCS. However, other potential confounders like disease duration or specific JME sub-syndromes were not included in the model.

items.evidence_snippet: Independent variables in the model were current use of levetiracetam, current use of valproate, current use of lamotrigine, gender, and age.
items.reasoning: Basic confounders (age, gender) were measured, but others like epilepsy duration or lifestyle factors were not in the model.
